messages:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selection tweak (auto->mixed-quant) we're seeing a perf regression on speculative decoding when pairing Llama variants with Mixtral drafts. p95 latency up and acceptance rate down.

taylor: ack, saw alerts. can you paste the quick numbers?

maria: p50 ~ 95ms -> 120ms, p95 110ms -> 210ms, acceptance_rate (speculative) 0.72 -> 0.44 on mixtral-8x paired with llama-13b-draft. kv_hit_rate dropped from 0.86 -> 0.59.

kai: interesting — sounds like KV alignment issue. did the kernel change alter KV layout or head ordering?

maria: kernel change selected mixed-quant path which uses a fused matmul kernel that expects head_dim ordering A/B (model-family agnostic). suspect mismatch in kv-reshape when pairing across families.

ash: quick repro I ran: single request trace attached.

ash: ```
TRACE: model_pair(lm=llama-13b,draft=mixtral-8x)
step=decode token=200
kernel=mixed-quant-fused
batch=1
kv_evictions=3
kv_hit_rate=0.58
latency_ms=234
acceptance=0
```

maria: that's the one. acceptance=0 for a lot of tokens then fallback kicks in, adds latency.

taylor: does the tokenizer differ? I remember mixtral uses subtle bytepair nuances, which can change prefix matches and speculative acceptance.

maria: tokenizer mismatch is real but we observed the hit even when tokenization was normalized. primary signal points to KV indexing and rope scaling differences. RoPE scaling leads to different phase offsets -> cache keys differ across families.

kai: ah that makes sense. If RoPE scaling is different, KV cache keys (the seq-pos embeddings folded into keys) won't align, so prefix caching and speculative accept checks fail.

sam: what was the acceptance threshold? we tune acceptance_rate threshold per-family last quarter to 0.7 default.

maria: acceptance threshold is 0.65. With current kernel mismatch acceptance drops to ~0.4.

taylor: two proposals: 1) short-term rollback of mixed-quant kernel for cross-family draft pairing routes; 2) add per-pairing KV normalization step in serving runtime: detect family mismatch and remap/scale RoPE keys to a canonical space before cache lookup.

kai: also consider expanding batching heuristics: when pairing families, force smaller batch windows to reduce the number of misaligned caches and avoid large evictions. Might increase cost but reduce p95.

ash: ran small patch that adds a RoPE scale-normalizer before kv key hash: acceptance_rate -> 0.71 and p95 down to 125ms on my test machine. Patch is in my branch: github.com/redwood/inference/patches/rope-normalize (internal).

maria: awesome — can you share the micro-profiling? where's the added CPU/GPU cost?

ash: extra ~2ms CPU per request for normalization + negligible GPU kernel time. Overall cost delta small compared to 90ms regression we saw.

taylor: good. runtime-bot, can you schedule a canary with rope-normalize enabled for cross-family routes only? 5% traffic for 2 hours, metrics: p95 latency, acceptance_rate, kv_hit_rate, cost_per_token.

runtime-bot: scheduled canary: route=pairing-crossfamily, rollout=5%, duration=120m, notify=#eng-runtime. Monitoring: p50/p95, acceptance_rate, kv_hit_rate, cpu_ms, gpu_ms.

sam: one more thing — tokenizer mismatch still contributes. let's also add a per-pairing tokenizer hash in routing metadata so we prefer drafts with identical tokenizer family when latency SLO is tight. fallback to normalized tokenization for lower-cost routes.

kai: +1. We'll need a small change in routing policy: prefer routes where tokenizer_hash == base_hash if latency sensitivity flag is on.

maria: action items: 1) ash open PR with tests and perf numbers (you already did) 2) taylor/ops run canary and watch metrics 3) kai add routing policy tweak and tokenizer_hash to model-catalog 4) sam update acceptance threshold docs for cross-family pairing.

taylor: I'll own canary. starting now. link to canary dashboard: https://console.redwood/metrics/canary/1830456789

maria: thanks — let's sync after 2h and decide rollback vs permanent change. :thumbsup:

sam: flagged a follow-up: create a short eval set to monitor acceptance regressions per model pair weekly.

kai: noted. also I'll add a small kernel-selection guard: if pairing.family_mismatch == true then disallow mixed-quant fused kernel until we have canonicalization enabled.

maria: perfect. closing loop after canary results.
